issues.legal_issue: A party is barred by res judicata from pursuing a special-leave appeal against an underlying tribunal decision when a final, unappealed High Court judgment has already decided the same dispute on its merits.
material_facts: After the revenue authority refused restitution of possession, the affected party challenged that decision before the High Court under Article 226.
The High Court dismissed the challenge after considering its merits, and the party did not appeal that judgment or otherwise seek to have it reversed.
The party later sought special leave to appeal directly against the underlying revenue authority’s decision, thereby seeking relief that would effectively undermine the final High Court judgment.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was barred by res judicata and was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle in Daryao v. State of U.P., a High Court decision dismissing a petition under Article 226 on its merits binds the parties unless modified or reversed in appeal or other appropriate proceedings. That principle applies a fortiori to an appeal under Article 136, where relief is discretionary. Indian Aluminium Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, West Bengal supports the same approach. Chandi Prasad Chokhani v. State of Bihar was explained as not displacing Daryao: the observations suggesting discretion to waive the rule were obiter, and the preliminary objection was upheld there as well.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_against_underlying_decision and prior_high_court_merits_decision and same_dispute and prior_decision_unreversed and appeal_bypasses_prior_decision

predicates.special_leave_appeal_against_underlying_: A party seeks special leave to appeal against an underlying tribunal or authority decision.
predicates.prior_high_court_merits_decision: The High Court has already decided the merits of the same dispute between the parties.
predicates.same_dispute: The later appeal concerns the dispute and relief addressed in the High Court proceeding.
predicates.prior_decision_unreversed: The High Court judgment has not been modified or reversed through appeal or another appropriate proceeding.
predicates.appeal_bypasses_prior_decision: The later appeal seeks relief that would effectively avoid or undermine the final High Court judgment.

issues.definition: When a party seeks special leave to appeal an underlying decision in the same dispute after an unreversed High Court merits judgment, and the appeal would bypass that judgment, the appeal is barred.
